raw_response:
Looking at my land and what I know from farming here my whole life — Quzhou is wheat-corn country. Every family on my lane does the same rotation. My mother did it, her mother did it. The soil here on the North China Plain is good for it, and the cooperative sells the seeds, the water is available from the village well shaft. I don't have money to experiment.

My husband is working in Baoding this year, so I'm managing alone with help from my older son during busy periods. I have about 5 mu of contracted land. I'll plant all of it in wheat starting October, then after harvest in June I'll seed corn directly into the stubble — saves me the ploughing cost and everyone in the village is doing it that way now.

For seeds I'll go to the village supply station and buy whatever improved wheat variety they're pushing — probably Jimai or Shiluan series, they give better yield than the old grain I used to save. Same for corn, I'll get hybrid seed, probably Zhengdan 958, it's what my neighbor uses and he gets good ears.

Fertilizer: I put down a lot because I'm scared of poor yield. I apply compound fertilizer as base, then urea top-dressing at jointing for wheat, and urea again for corn at the big bell stage. I know the extension people say I use too much nitrogen but I'd rather have a bit extra than fall short.

Irrigation: wheat needs 3-4 waterings here — sowing water, winter freeze water, jointing, and heading. Corn I'll water at planting if it's dry, and at tasseling. We pay per hour of pump time so I try not to over-irrigate, but I won't risk drought stress.

Pesticides: for wheat I'll spray herbicide in autumn and then one fungicide pass for powdery mildew in spring. For corn I'll do a herbicide after emergence and watch for corn borer — spray if I see it.
